By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by the Career Com­
pensation Act of 1949, approved October 
12, 1949 (Public Law 351—81st Cong.), 
it is ordered that the last paragraph of 
Executive Order No. 10084 of October 12, 
1949, entitled “Prescribing Regulations 
for the Administration of Certain Pro­
visions of the Career Compensation Act 
of 1949”, be, and it is hereby, amended to 
read as follows:
114 P. R. 6245.
“This order shall take effect on Oc­
tober 1, 1949, and shall cease to be ef­
fective on March 31, 1950.”

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 10098 (15 FR 461 (Federal Register of January 27, 1950)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10098 was signed January 25, 1950. Its only command amends the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 to read that the order takes effect October 1, 1949 and ceases to be effective on March 31, 1950, replacing the January 31, 1950 sunset. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

No instrument ends the parent order before January 31, 1951, and no end on a date between amendments is shown, because each amendment takes effect the day after the preceding date.","independent_command_check":"The clause has one function, which is to fix the duration of the adoption of regulations in Executive Order No. 10084, and has no separate command. The listed sections are separately sunsetted by the amendments, but the parent order as a whole ends when the last of them ends, which is the date recorded.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. savings_residuals.reason: The order's text has no saving clause. Pay and allowances earned under the regulations while they were adopted are entitlements under the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and the regulations then in force; the held text creates no continuing duty after January 31, 1951, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the adoption.
